whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as 6 months if a government entity was involved.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible — your share of fault simply reduces the amount, not the right to pursue it.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Don't Pay Upfront

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Watsonville?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you 2 years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government agency was involved, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes only 6 months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means being partly at fault doesn't stop you from recovering compensation. Your percentage of fault would reduce the amount you might receive, but it doesn't eliminate your ability to pursue a claim.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Watsonville?
items.answer: Based on public-record collision counts, higher volumes have been reported along Main Street, Freedom Boulevard, Green Valley Road, and Airport Boulevard, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply reported patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.
